Senior Product Managers — Four High-Impact Opportunities at Finom

Product · Full-time · Remote

About Finom

Finom is building the financial operating system for European entrepreneurs and SMEs—bringing banking, payments, invoicing, accounting and financial management together in one platform.
We’re hiring four Senior Product Managers across some of our most important product areas:
 
Risk Intelligence
 
Customer Experience — Trust & Risk
 
Activation & Growth
 
Integrations
Each role has a distinct mission, but all four offer genuine end-to-end ownership. You’ll define the problem, shape the strategy, work directly with customers and cross-functional partners, and remain close to execution until your work is delivering measurable customer and commercial impact.
We prototype and learn quickly, including using AI tools to test ideas before committing significant engineering time. Our Product Managers partner with Engineering, Design and Data as peers—and are expected to make the commercial case for what they build, not simply manage a backlog.⁠⁠​
 

The opportunities

1. Senior Product Manager — Risk Intelligence

You’ll lead the cross-functional squad responsible for the risk signals and eligibility decisions that Finom’s products depend on.
As Finom expands into areas such as credit, savings and payment acceptance, we need a centralised risk and eligibility platform that can support multiple products without slowing them down. You’ll shape this platform from an early stage—defining its vision, architecture, roadmap and commercial impact.
What you’ll be doing
 
Own the strategy, roadmap and outcomes of the Risk Intelligence squad.
 
Define and build Finom’s central risk and eligibility platform.
 
Shape how credit, savings, payment acceptance and future products consume risk capabilities.
 
Turn complex risk, data and compliance requirements into scalable product components and interfaces.
 
Partner closely with Engineering, Machine Learning and Risk teams.
 
Design experiments that demonstrate the engine’s impact on revenue, risk and customer outcomes.
 
Keep existing risk signals reliable while building the platform’s next generation.
Why join this team?
This is not a maintenance or delivery role. You’ll help create a multi-product platform that does not yet exist, with significant autonomy and visibility across Product leadership, regulators and potentially the board. It is a rare opportunity to define how risk decisioning works inside a fast-growing European fintech.⁠⁠​
The skill set we’re looking for
 
Experience owning a risk engine, decisioning, scoring or eligibility product.
 
Risk-product experience across multiple products or a genuinely complex platform.
 
Strong systems thinking, including components, APIs and cross-product dependencies.
 
Confidence working with model-performance metrics and experiment design.
 
The ability to challenge Engineering, Data and ML partners with evidence.
 
Experience operating in a regulated, ambiguous and rapidly changing environment.
 
An AI-native, hands-on approach to product management.
Experience with EU AML requirements, decision-engine platforms or hands-on ML and analytics would be valuable, but is not essential.
 

2. Senior Product Manager — Customer Experience, Trust & Risk

You’ll lead the squad responsible for how customers experience Finom’s risk and compliance interventions.
Document requests, payment verification, transaction holds, limits and account closures are among the most stressful moments in a customer’s relationship with a financial platform. Your mission will be to ensure that customers understand what is happening, know what to do next and reach a resolution as quickly as possible.
What you’ll be doing
 
Own the customer experience of risk and compliance interventions across web and mobile.
 
Lead the Customer Experience squad’s strategy, roadmap and outcomes.
 
Replace fragmented emails and forms with clearer, increasingly conversational and AI-native experiences.
 
Build shared customer-experience infrastructure that other Trust & Risk teams can use.
 
Speak directly with customers to understand friction, confusion and silent churn.
 
Define metrics connecting intervention friction with satisfaction, NPS and retention.
 
Align Risk, Compliance, Operations, Customer Care, Engineering, AI and Data around shared solutions.
 
Balance customer empathy with non-negotiable AML and regulatory requirements.
Why join this team?
This is a horizontal role with impact across the entire Trust & Risk domain. You’ll own the moments when customer trust is most vulnerable—and have the opportunity to transform necessary compliance interventions into experiences that are clear, fair and fast.⁠⁠​
The skill set we’re looking for
 
Strong customer-experience craft, including journeys, messaging, edge cases and service recovery.
 
Experience shipping products for high-stakes or emotionally charged customer moments.
 
A record of taking products from discovery through to launch and measurable impact.
 
Strong stakeholder leadership across complex team boundaries.
 
The ability to create a measurement system from scratch and use it to guide decisions.
 
Customer discovery skills grounded in direct conversations and behavioural data.
 
Comfort designing within regulatory or operational constraints.
 
A practical, AI-native approach to prototyping and shipping.
Experience in trust and safety, financial crime prevention, disputes, collections or conversational AI would be particularly useful.
 

3. Senior Product Manager — Activation & Growth

You’ll focus on turning newly onboarded customers into engaged, retained Finom users.
The challenge is not simply getting someone through registration. It is helping each entrepreneur reach meaningful value quickly—whether that means issuing a card, receiving a payment, sending an invoice or making Finom part of their everyday financial workflow.
What you’ll be doing
 
Own key parts of the customer activation and early-retention journey.
 
Define what meaningful activation looks like for different customer segments.
 
Identify and remove friction across onboarding and the first product experience.
 
Build a structured experimentation roadmap across customer journeys, messaging and product education.
 
Use behavioural data and customer research to identify the highest-impact growth opportunities.
 
Develop personalised and contextual experiences that guide customers towards their next best action.
 
Partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing and CRM teams.
 
Connect activation improvements to retention, revenue and long-term customer value.
Why join this team?
You’ll work on one of the clearest drivers of Finom’s growth: helping more entrepreneurs experience the platform’s value and continue using it. This is an opportunity to influence the full customer journey, run meaningful experiments and see a direct connection between your decisions and company growth.⁠⁠⁠⁠​
The skill set we’re looking for
 
Strong experience in product-led growth, activation, onboarding or retention.
 
A record of improving measurable funnel and customer-behaviour outcomes.
 
Deep understanding of experimentation, including hypotheses, success metrics and guardrails.
 
Strong quantitative judgment combined with qualitative customer insight.
 
Experience designing personalised journeys or behavioural growth loops.
 
The ability to move between strategy, hands-on discovery and rapid delivery.
 
Commercial thinking—you understand how customer behaviour connects to revenue and lifetime value.
 
Experience working in a fast-moving, cross-functional product environment.
Fintech, subscription, marketplace or B2B SaaS experience would be useful, but evidence of driving activation and retention at scale matters most.
 

4. Senior Product Manager — Integrations

You’ll help make Finom more valuable by connecting it with the wider financial and business software ecosystem used by European SMEs.
Our customers rely on accounting platforms, payment providers and other operational tools. Your role will be to make the movement of financial data between those systems reliable, scalable and easy to understand.
What you’ll be doing
 
Own the strategy and roadmap for Finom’s integrations ecosystem.
 
Identify the integrations that will create the greatest customer and commercial value.
 
Lead integrations with accounting platforms, financial partners and third-party providers.
 
Define reusable platform capabilities rather than building each integration as a one-off.
 
Work with Engineering on APIs, data flows, reliability and technical trade-offs.
 
Partner with external providers and influence their roadmaps when required.
 
Improve how customers discover, configure and use integrations.
 
Define metrics covering adoption, reliability, customer value and commercial impact.
Why join this team?
Integrations are central to Finom’s ambition to become the financial operating system for European SMEs. You’ll help turn Finom from a standalone product into the connected centre of a customer’s financial stack—combining technical platform work, customer discovery and strategic partnerships.⁠⁠⁠⁠​
The skill set we’re looking for
 
Experience delivering integrations, APIs, platform products or technically complex B2B products.
 
Confidence working with engineers on data flows, system boundaries and integration trade-offs.
 
Strong product judgment: you can separate high-value ecosystem opportunities from low-impact requests.
 
Experience working with external partners and managing dependencies outside your direct control.
 
The ability to learn complex new domains quickly and drive progress through ambiguity.
 
Strong customer discovery and commercial prioritisation skills.
 
A hands-on mentality and willingness to remain close to delivery.
 
Clear communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Previous accounting-software or fintech integration experience is valuable, but we are equally interested in highly driven platform Product Managers who can learn the domain quickly.
 

What all four roles have in common

We’re looking for Senior Product Managers who:
 
Own outcomes, not just roadmaps or delivery plans.
 
Talk directly to customers and use data to test their assumptions.
 
Can move comfortably between strategy and hands-on execution.
 
Prototype and validate ideas quickly, including through AI-assisted workflows.
 
Partner with Engineering, Design and Data rather than handing over requirements.
 
Create clarity and alignment without waiting for someone else to do it.
 
Understand the commercial impact of their product decisions.
 
Are comfortable making decisions in a fast-changing scale-up environment.
You won’t be expected to choose between the four opportunities without context. During the interview process, we’ll explore your strengths, interests and experience, introduce you to the relevant leaders, and identify where you can have the greatest impact.⁠⁠​

Ready to build with us?

If you want to own a meaningful product area, work closely with strong cross-functional teams and build products that help European entrepreneurs spend less time on financial administration, we’d love to hear from you.
Apply to our Senior Product Manager opportunity and tell us which product area interests you most—or let’s work that out together.

Senior Reconciliation Analyst (Fixed-Term Cover)

About the Role
Our Reconciliation team makes sure that every euro our clients see in their balances is actually backed by cash in the bank — and right now, we need an experienced Senior Reconciliation Analyst to join us on a fixed-term basis to cover a period of maternity leave.
This is a hands-on, high-impact role at the heart of our payment operations. You'll own the day-to-day routine of monitoring reconciliation breaks, investigating discrepancies, and working closely with engineering and banking partners to keep everything balanced. It's a fast-moving environment where priorities can shift daily, so we're looking for someone who thrives on structure one day and adapts the next.
While the core focus is routine reconciliation, there's real room to get involved in automation projects once you're up to speed — and this role can also be a strong stepping stone into other teams at the company longer-term.
A Bit About the Team
Our Reconciliation team is small but mighty — every analyst is expected to think like an owner, gradually automating routine work while keeping the core process rock-solid. It's a team that values flexibility (fully remote, outcome-focused — we care that the job gets done, not what hours you keep) and gives people real autonomy once the fundamentals are covered. If you enjoy solving problems that sit right at the intersection of data and payments, you'll fit right in here.
About the Role
Our Reconciliation team makes sure that every euro our clients see in their balances is actually backed by cash in the bank — and right now, we need an experienced Senior Reconciliation Analyst to join us on a fixed-term basis to cover a period of maternity leave.
This is a hands-on, high-impact role at the heart of our payment operations. You'll own the day-to-day routine of monitoring reconciliation breaks, investigating discrepancies, and working closely with engineering and banking partners to keep everything balanced. It's a fast-moving environment where priorities can shift daily, so we're looking for someone who thrives on structure one day and adapts the next.
While the core focus is routine reconciliation, there's real room to get involved in automation projects once you're up to speed — and this role can also be a strong stepping stone into other teams at the company longer-term.

What You Will Be Doing
Own daily reconciliation monitoring — checking that cash held in the bank matches client balances in our systems, and flagging and investigating any breaks or mismatches as they arise
Resolve reconciliation breaks end-to-end — determining whether an issue is internal (looping in engineering) or external (liaising directly with banks and third-party payment providers) and driving it to resolution
Maintain reporting and month-end close — supporting vendor reporting, regulatory reporting, and other recurring reporting cycles with a high level of accuracy
Work across data tools — using Excel alongside data visualization tools (Databricks, Metabase, or similar — Tableau/Power BI experience also welcome) to monitor and track reconciliation data
Contribute to automation — gradually helping automate manual reconciliation processes using AI and other tools, reducing reliance on spreadsheets over time
Handle occasional manual money transfers — with the accuracy and attention to detail this requires
Manage stakeholders across the business — working with engineering, treasury, and external banking partners to keep processes running smoothly

Who You Are
You have hands-on experience in reconciliation, payment operations, or treasury operations (e.g. as a reconciliation specialist, payment analyst, or accountant with reconciliation exposure)
You're comfortable with Excel and have some experience with data visualization/BI tools (Databricks, Metabase, Tableau, Power BI, or similar)
You have a working understanding of payment schemes and how money moves between banks and internal systems — you know who to go to when something doesn't add up
You're diligent and detail-oriented, especially when it comes to handling money movements
You're used to fast-paced, frequently changing environments and can adapt when processes shift — this isn't a role with a fixed rulebook
You have strong stakeholder management skills and are confident communicating with both internal teams and external partners (e.g. banks)
You're able to start immediately or on very short notice
You're open to a fixed-term contract (~5 months, with a real possibility of extension depending on business needs)

Nice to Have
Experience working at a neobank or fintech (e.g. N26 or similar) — you'll likely need less ramp-up time in a high-change environment
A mathematical or quantitative background
Prior experience helping build or improve automations within a reconciliation or payments workflow
Basic SQL or data analysis skills

A Bit About the Team

Our Reconciliation team is small but mighty — every analyst is expected to think like an owner, gradually automating routine work while keeping the core process rock-solid. It's a team that values flexibility (fully remote, outcome-focused — we care that the job gets done, not what hours you keep) and gives people real autonomy once the fundamentals are covered. If you enjoy solving problems that sit right at the intersection of data and payments, you'll fit right in here.

About the Role

Our Reconciliation team makes sure that every euro our clients see in their balances is actually backed by cash in the bank — and right now, we need an experienced Senior Reconciliation Analyst to join us on a fixed-term basis to cover a period of maternity leave.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role at the heart of our payment operations. You'll own the day-to-day routine of monitoring reconciliation breaks, investigating discrepancies, and working closely with engineering and banking partners to keep everything balanced. It's a fast-moving environment where priorities can shift daily, so we're looking for someone who thrives on structure one day and adapts the next.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Maintain reporting and month-end close — supporting vendor reporting, regulatory reporting, and other recurring reporting cycles with a high level of accuracy
  • Work across data tools — using Excel alongside data visualization tools (Databricks, Metabase, or similar — Tableau/Power BI experience also welcome) to monitor and track reconciliation data
  • Contribute to automation — gradually helping automate manual reconciliation processes using AI and other tools, reducing reliance on spreadsheets over time
  • Handle occasional manual money transfers — with the accuracy and attention to detail this requires
  • Manage stakeholders across the business — working with engineering, treasury, and external banking partners to keep processes running smoothly

Who You Are

  • You have hands-on experience in reconciliation, payment operations, or treasury operations (e.g. as a reconciliation specialist, payment analyst, or accountant with reconciliation exposure)

  • You have strong stakeholder management skills and are confident communicating with both internal teams and external partners (e.g. banks)
  • You're able to start immediately or on very short notice
  • You're open to a fixed-term contract (~5 months, with a real possibility of extension depending on business needs)

Nice to Have

  • Experience working at a neobank or fintech (e.g. N26 or similar) — you'll likely need less ramp-up time in a high-change environment
  • A mathematical or quantitative background
  • Prior experience helping build or improve automations within a reconciliation or payments workflow
  • Basic SQL or data analysis skills

descriptionPlain:
About Finom
 
Finom is a European tech startup headquartered in Amsterdam, and we’re on a journey towards revolutionizing the financial landscape for entrepreneurs worldwide. Our mission is to develop an all-in-one financial B2B solution that integrates banking functions, accounting, financial management, and invoicing into a seamless, mobile-first platform.
 
We recently closed a €115 million Series C equity round (around $133 million), bringing our total funding to approximately $346 million. This significant investment follows a $105 million growth funding round from General Catalyst, a long-term backer since 2021 known for supporting companies like Airbnb, HubSpot, KAYAK, and Stripe.
 
Finom's platform goes beyond traditional banking, offering invoicing and a growing suite of features, including AI-enabled accounting, aiming to simplify financial management for entrepreneurs. We're actively expanding our reach across key EU markets like Germany, France, the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain.
 
At Finom, we’re not just redefining the entrepreneurial experience — we’re empowering our employees to make a real difference. Your work matters, and your impact extends far beyond product metrics. We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.
 
Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.


We are looking for a Senior Treasury Manager to build and run Finom's treasury function.
Finom safeguards a significant book of customer funds across its regulated entities. Net interest income on that book is a meaningful revenue line, and it will grow. Today the function is up and running: the money is placed, the investment policy is in place, and a large part of the book sits with an external asset manager. What we are building now is the machinery around it — an evidenced limit framework, look-through into what our managers actually hold, automated investment accounting, and a reconciled NII number we can defend to an auditor and a regulator.
That is the job. You will take part in building it, and you will run it while it is being built.
This is a hands-on role at the intersection of regulation, liquidity, and commercial impact — not a back-office position. It suits someone who has done this before in a regulated environment and wants to do it again without four layers of committee above them.

We are looking for a Senior Treasury Manager to build and run Finom's treasury function.

Finom safeguards a significant book of customer funds across its regulated entities. Net interest income on that book is a meaningful revenue line, and it will grow. Today the function is up and running: the money is placed, the investment policy is in place, and a large part of the book sits with an external asset manager. lists.content:
Liquidity and funding

  • Daily liquidity positioning and float management across entities and accounts
  • Intraday funding of payment channels; nostro and correspondent account management
  • Collateral and minimum-balance obligations across card schemes, T2, and credit providers
  • Contingency funding — the playbook for the day we need €20m by tomorrow morning
  • A daily treasury balance sheet — net liquidity and net capital available — that reconciles

    • Safeguarding and portfolio

  • Portfolio management of safeguarded client funds: term deposits, MMFs, short-dated debt, held directly and via external managers
  • Safeguarding adequacy: shortfall detection, top-up execution, same-currency discipline
  • Instrument eligibility screening under CRR risk-weight, maturity and WAL constraints, and UCITS/MMF rules
  • Independent, evidenced validation that externally managed allocations sit inside mandate — position-level look-through, daily monitoring of concentration, maturity, WAL and credit quality, breach escalation
  • NII forecasting, attribution, and reconciled performance reporting; treasury inputs into the financial model and company forecast

    • Governance and controls

  • Ownership of the investment policy, limit framework, and eligible-instrument register
  • Treasury governance: decision pack, agenda, decision log, and delegated-authority register
  • Pre-deal checks and post-trade evidencing, designed so that the first line executes and the second line challenges
  • Covenant tracking across credit facilities
  • Regulator, external audit, and second-line engagement on treasury and safeguarding matters

    • Systems and data

  • Selection and implementation of investment accounting and treasury tooling — a Clearwater/Advent-class implementation is already in flight and will be yours
  • Custodian, asset-manager and bank data feeds; API connectivity where it exists and pragmatic alternatives where it doesn't
  • Replacing manual spreadsheet processes with something that survives your holiday

    • Commercial

  • Bank, custodian, broker and asset-manager relationships: onboarding, commercial terms, mandate setting, service review
  • Challenging our managers on allocation, transparency and fees — and changing them if the answers are weak

lists.text: What good looks like in the first 12 months
lists.content:
• Investment policy and limit framework live, with treasury governance running on a documented decision log
  • Daily, evidenced mandate compliance across the full book — we can answer "are we inside the boundaries?" in minutes, not weeks
  • Investment accounting platform implemented; monthly close on the portfolio no longer manual
  • An NII number that is reconciled, attributed, and forecastable
  • A contingency liquidity playbook that has been tested rather than written

• 5+ years in treasury, ALM, fixed income, or portfolio management at a regulated financial institution, EMI/PI, or asset manager
  • Direct experience with client money or safeguarding under PSD2 / EMD — core to this role, not adjacent to it
  • Experience building or materially rebuilding a treasury function, not only operating inside an established one
  • Strong command of bond math, yield and duration, MMF mechanics, and credit and concentration risk at instrument level
  • Track record of automating manual treasury processes and implementing treasury or investment accounting systems
  • Comfortable working with position-level data directly — you can interrogate a portfolio file rather than wait for a report
  • Experience with regulators, external audit, and external asset managers (mandate setting, IMA terms, performance challenge)
  • Sound judgement under time pressure in a lean environment with real accountability and limited cover
  • Strong Excel skills
  • Fluent English
    •  

    Nice to have

  • Familiarity with IFRS 9 or Dutch GAAP (RJ 290) financial instrument accounting
  • SQL or Python
  • Experience in a firm transitioning toward a banking licence
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g. LLMs, copilots) to accelerate analytical and reporting workflows

descriptionBody:
We are looking for a Senior Treasury Manager to build and run Finom's treasury function.

Finom safeguards a significant book of customer funds across its regulated entities. Net interest income on that book is a meaningful revenue line, and it will grow. Today the function is up and running: the money is placed, the investment policy is in place, and a large part of the book sits with an external asset manager. What we are building now is the machinery around it — an evidenced limit framework, look-through into what our managers actually hold, automated investment accounting, and a reconciled NII number we can defend to an auditor and a regulator.

That is the job. You will take part in building it, and you will run it while it is being built.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of regulation, liquidity, and commercial impact — not a back-office position. It suits someone who has done this before in a regulated environment and wants to do it again without four layers of committee above them.

Target2 Process Owner
Location: Netherlands, Spain, Cyprus or Poland
Or: freelance agreement in other countries (CEST time zone or adjacent preferred)
Job description
We are hiring a T2 Process Owner to own the operational side of this transition end to end. This is a hands-on, dedicated role: you will set up every Payment Operations process required for direct participation, maintain the operational infrastructure once live, and be the operational point of contact for the T2 scheme, DNB and partner banks.
Your remit spans the full lifecycle: designing and documenting the operating model before go-live, validating it in the August end-to-end UAT, cutting over BIC by BIC, and maintaining it as business-as-usual.
Payment operations processes
Recalls — own incoming and outgoing SCT Inst recalls end to end, including the alert/customer-consent flow and full/partial refund outcomes.
Inquiries and investigations — automate and support SCT/SCT Inst payment investigations directly with the scheme, including non-receipt investigations and pacs.028 status requests.
SWIFT / ISO 20022 — own and automate SWIFT enquiry handling (MT199/MT999, RFIs) and pacs/camt/pain flows.
Incoming/missing funds — own inbound RTGS monitoring, exception-handling and returns; confirm payments settle correctly, manage unmatched items and Escrow infrastructure.
Rejects, returns and refunds — maintain decision and customer-handling processes, back-office visibility, codes and alerts.
T2 platform and infrastructure
Operate and own the T2 GUI/dashboard (U2A and A2A) as senior authorised user — tracking, returns, liquidity visibility, fallback/manual actions.
Maintain CRDM reference data (BICs, routing, accounts, users, roles, certificates), the TARGET authorization matrix and segregation of duties, and the manual-vs-automated split.
Manage the dual-route transition from indirect to direct participation, ensuring traceability by BIC and payment path, and define retirement criteria for each BNPP-dependent step.
Own the Payment Ops interface into daily reconciliation across MCA, RTGS DCA and TIPS DCA, escalating where liquidity affects execution or customers.
Incident management, contingency and reporting
Redesign the incident process for direct participation, replacing BNPP escalation with DNB/FIS/TARGET routes.
Own the Payment Ops role in DNB notifications and reporting, retaining evidence to DNB readiness standard.
Define the Payment Ops role in the Eurosystem contingency solution (ECONS II), including training and test evidence.
Cross-functional and external coordination
Act as operational point of contact for DNB, SWIFT/NSP (NEXI), FIS, and other banks/correspondents (including BNP Paribas during dual-run).
Partner with Product and Engineering: test interfaces, define what stays automated vs. manual — these decisions sit with Ops.
Work closely with the reconciliation team on liquidity management.
What success looks like
Every process has a named owner, documented delta from existing process, confirmed manual/automated steps, agreed escalation/fallback, and passing UAT evidence.
Full set of T2 procedures established: recalls, investigations/pacs.028, inbound RTGS/Escrow returns, rejects, reconciliation, incident and GUI fallback.
Successful migration to direct participation with zero impact on customer experience and accurate Customer Support guidance.
Post-go-live: stable BAU with Finom-controlled SLAs and no residual BNPP dependency.
Requirements
3+ years in payment operations at a bank, EMI or PSP, with hands-on exposure to SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst) and TARGET Services (T2/RTGS, TIPS) direct connectivity.
Working knowledge of investigations, recalls, returns/refunds, and SWIFT/ISO 20022 messaging (MT199/MT999, pacs/camt/pain).
Comfortable operating central-infrastructure interfaces hands-on (T2 GUI, CRDM, reconciliation/liquidity tools), including U2A/A2A actions.
Strong process design and documentation skills — SOPs, four-eyes controls, authorization matrices, audit-quality evidence.
Confidence coordinating with regulators and external parties, and translating operational needs to Product and Engineering.
Senior enough to own sign-offs, incident escalation and DNB-reporting decisions independently, across Ops, IT/Security, Compliance, Risk and Finance Ops.
Familiarity with DNB/TARGET-NL conditions, IPR and EMI/PSD2 operational obligations.
Professional fluency in English.
Nice to have
Prior involvement in a direct TARGET/RTGS/TIPS onboarding or sponsor-bank-to-direct-participation migration.
Experience standing up incident management and contingency (ECONS II) processes.

Location: Netherlands, Spain, Cyprus or Poland

Job description

We are hiring a T2 Process Owner to own the operational side of this transition end to end. This is a hands-on, dedicated role: you will set up every Payment Operations process required for direct participation, maintain the operational infrastructure once live, and be the operational point of contact for the T2 scheme, DNB and partner banks.

Your remit spans the full lifecycle: designing and documenting the operating model before go-live, validating it in the August end-to-end UAT, cutting over BIC by BIC, and maintaining it as business-as-usual.

Payment operations processes

  • Recalls — own incoming and outgoing SCT Inst recalls end to end, including the alert/customer-consent flow and full/partial refund outcomes.
  • Inquiries and investigations — automate and support SCT/SCT Inst payment investigations directly with the scheme, including non-receipt investigations and pacs.028 status requests.
  • SWIFT / ISO 20022 — own and automate SWIFT enquiry handling (MT199/MT999, RFIs) and pacs/camt/pain flows.
  • Incoming/missing funds — own inbound RTGS monitoring, exception-handling and returns; confirm payments settle correctly, manage unmatched items and Escrow infrastructure.
  • Rejects, returns and refunds — maintain decision and customer-handling processes, back-office visibility, codes and alerts.

T2 platform and infrastructure

  • Operate and own the T2 GUI/dashboard (U2A and A2A) as senior authorised user — tracking, returns, liquidity visibility, fallback/manual actions.
  • Maintain CRDM reference data (BICs, routing, accounts, users, roles, certificates), the TARGET authorization matrix and segregation of duties, and the manual-vs-automated split.
  • Manage the dual-route transition from indirect to direct participation, ensuring traceability by BIC and payment path, and define retirement criteria for each BNPP-dependent step.
  • Own the Payment Ops interface into daily reconciliation across MCA, RTGS DCA and TIPS DCA, escalating where liquidity affects execution or customers.

Incident management, contingency and reporting

  • Redesign the incident process for direct participation, replacing BNPP escalation with DNB/FIS/TARGET routes.
  • Own the Payment Ops role in DNB notifications and reporting, retaining evidence to DNB readiness standard.
  • Define the Payment Ops role in the Eurosystem contingency solution (ECONS II), including training and test evidence.

Cross-functional and external coordination

  • Act as operational point of contact for DNB, SWIFT/NSP (NEXI), FIS, and other banks/correspondents (including BNP Paribas during dual-run).
  • Partner with Product and Engineering: test interfaces, define what stays automated vs. manual — these decisions sit with Ops.
  • Work closely with the reconciliation team on liquidity management.

What success looks like

  • Every process has a named owner, documented delta from existing process, confirmed manual/automated steps, agreed escalation/fallback, and passing UAT evidence.
  • Full set of T2 procedures established: recalls, investigations/pacs.028, inbound RTGS/Escrow returns, rejects, reconciliation, incident and GUI fallback.
  • Successful migration to direct participation with zero impact on customer experience and accurate Customer Support guidance.
  • Post-go-live: stable BAU with Finom-controlled SLAs and no residual BNPP dependency.

Requirements

  • 3+ years in payment operations at a bank, EMI or PSP, with hands-on exposure to SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst) and TARGET Services (T2/RTGS, TIPS) direct connectivity.
  • Working knowledge of investigations, recalls, returns/refunds, and SWIFT/ISO 20022 messaging (MT199/MT999, pacs/camt/pain).
  • Comfortable operating central-infrastructure interfaces hands-on (T2 GUI, CRDM, reconciliation/liquidity tools), including U2A/A2A actions.
  • Strong process design and documentation skills — SOPs, four-eyes controls, authorization matrices, audit-quality evidence.
  • Confidence coordinating with regulators and external parties, and translating operational needs to Product and Engineering.
  • Senior enough to own sign-offs, incident escalation and DNB-reporting decisions independently, across Ops, IT/Security, Compliance, Risk and Finance Ops.
  • Familiarity with DNB/TARGET-NL conditions, IPR and EMI/PSD2 operational obligations.
  • Professional fluency in English.

Nice to have

  • Prior involvement in a direct TARGET/RTGS/TIPS onboarding or sponsor-bank-to-direct-participation migration.
  • Experience standing up incident management and contingency (ECONS II) processes.

  • Own the Payment Ops role in DNB notifications and reporting (settlement mismatches, operational incidents) and retain evidence to the DNB readiness standard.
  • Define the Payment Ops role in the Eurosystem contingency solution (ECONS II) for severe TARGET disruption, including training and test evidence.

Cross-functional and external coordination

  • Work directly with the T2 scheme / Eurosystem on certification, registration and reference data, and act as an operational point of contact for DNB, SWIFT / the NSP (NEXI) and the FIS service provider.
  • Handle communications with other banks and correspondents, including BNP Paribas during the dual-run period.
  • Partner directly with the Product and Engineering teams: test interfaces, identify back-office development needs from dashboard testing, and specify what stays automated versus manual — you are the operational voice defining how the platform must behave, and these decisions sit with Ops, not with engineering.
  • Work closely with our reconciliation team on liquidity management and forming operational processes around it

What success looks like

  • Every Payment Ops process for direct participation has a named owner, a documented existing-process-plus-T2-delta, confirmed manual/automated steps, agreed escalation and fallback, and passing UAT evidence, meeting regulatory and customer expectations
  • Full set of T2 procedures established and ownership → recalls, investigations/pacs.028, inbound RTGS credit and Escrow return, rejects, reconciliation, incident and GUI fallback
  • Successful migration from indirect participation to direct, withdocumented and Customer Support equipped with accurate customer-facing guidance, and 0 impact on customer experience
  • Post-go-live, T2 operations run as stable BAU with Finom-controlled investigation SLAs and no residual BNPP operational dependency.

Requirements

  • Experience in payment operations at a bank, EMI or PSP, ideally covering SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst) and TARGET Services with direct connectivity
  • Working knowledge of payment investigations, recalls, returns and SWIFT / ISO 20022 messaging (MT199/MT999, pacs/camt/pain).
  • Comfort operating central-infrastructure interfaces hands-on (T2 GUI, CRDM, reconciliation and liquidity-monitoring tools), including U2A/A2A actions.
  • Strong process design and documentation skills — able to author DNB-ready SOPs, define four-eyes controls and authorization matrices, and produce audit-quality evidence.
  • Confidence coordinating with regulators and external parties (DNB, Eurosystem, SWIFT/NSP, service providers, correspondent banks) and translating operational needs to Product and Engineering.
  • Senior enough to own sign-offs, incident escalation and DNB-reporting decisions independently, while working across Ops, IT/Security, Compliance, Risk and Finance Ops.
  • Familiarity with DNB / TARGET-NL conditions, IPR (Instant Payments Regulation) and EMI/PSD2 operational obligations.

Nice to have

  • Prior involvement in a direct TARGET / RTGS / TIPS onboarding or a sponsor-bank-to-direct-participation migration.
  • Experience standing up incident management and contingency (ECONS II) processes for payment infrastructure.

Prerequisites

  • Minimum 3+ years of experience in payment operations at a bank, EMI, or PSP, with hands-on exposure to SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst) and TARGET Services (T2/RTGS, TIPS) direct connectivity.
  • Practical knowledge of payment investigations, recalls, returns/refunds workflows, and SWIFT / ISO 20022 messaging standards (MT199/MT999, pacs, camt, pain).
  • Demonstrated experience operating central financial-infrastructure interfaces directly (e.g., T2 GUI, CRDM, reconciliation or liquidity-monitoring tools), including U2A/A2A actions.
  • Proven ability to design and document operational processes, including SOPs, four-eyes controls, and authorization matrices to audit/regulatory standard.
  • Experience liaising directly with regulators or scheme operators (e.g., central banks, Eurosystem, SWIFT/NSP) and cross-functional teams such as Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Risk.
  • Seniority sufficient to independently own sign-offs, incident escalation, and regulatory reporting decisions.
  • Familiarity with relevant regulatory frameworks — DNB/TARGET-NL conditions, the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), and EMI/PSD2 operational obligations.
  • Professional fluency in English (written and spoken) for regulatory and cross-border coordination.

This significant investment follows a $105 million growth funding round from General Catalyst, a long-term backer since 2021 known for supporting companies like Airbnb, HubSpot, KAYAK, and Stripe.
 
Finom's platform goes beyond traditional banking, offering invoicing and a growing suite of features, including AI-enabled accounting, aiming to simplify financial management for entrepreneurs. We're actively expanding our reach across key EU markets like Germany, France, the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain.
 
At Finom, we’re not just redefining the entrepreneurial experience — we’re empowering our employees to make a real difference. Your work matters, and your impact extends far beyond product metrics. We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.
 
Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.

T2 Process Owner

  • Location: Netherlands, Cyprus, Spain or Poland
  • Or: freelance agreement in other countries (CEST time zone (or adjacent) preferred)

Job description

We are hiring a T2 Process Owner to own the operational side of this transition end to end. This is a hands-on, dedicated role: you will set up every Payment Operations process required for direct participation, maintain the operational infrastructure once live, and be the operational point of contact for the T2 scheme, DNB and partner banks.

You own the operational set-up for T2 and the processes and infrastructure that keep it running. Your remit spans the full lifecycle: designing and documenting the operating model before go-live, validating it in the August end-to-end UAT, cutting over BIC by BIC, and then maintaining it as business-as-usual.

Payment operations processes

  • Recalls — own incoming and outgoing SCT Inst recalls end to end, including the alert/customer-consent flow and positive/negative outcomes with full and partial refunds.
  • SCT / SCT Inst inquiries and investigations — automate and support payment investigations directly with the scheme, including outgoing non-receipt investigations and pacs.028 payment-status requests
  • Incoming and outgoing SWIFT messages — own and automate SWIFT enquiry handling (MT199 / MT999, RFIs) and the relevant ISO 20022 flows (pacs, camt, pain)
  • Incoming / missing funds — own the inbound RTGS payment monitoring, exception-handling and return SOP: confirm correctly addressed payments settle and book automatically, handle unmatched/pending items and establishment of Escrow infrastructure, and be able to state with confidence whether a payment has or has not reached Finom.
  • Rejects, returns and refunds — maintain the operational decision and customer-handling processes; confirm back-office visibility, codes and alerts for abnormal exceptions.

T2 platform and operational infrastructure

  • Direct platform access — operate and own the T2 GUI / dashboard directly (U2A and A2A), as senior authorised user, for payment tracking, returns, liquidity visibility and fallback/manual actions.
  • Infrastructure maintenance — define and maintain the operational setup: CRDM reference-data maintenance (BICs, routing, accounts, users, roles, certificates), the TARGET access / four-eyes authorization matrix and production segregation of duties, and the manual-vs-automated split for day-one operations.
  • Dual-route transition — manage migration from indirect participation, ensuring every item is routable and traceable by BIC and payment path, and define the criteria for retiring each BNPP-dependent step.
  • Reconciliation and liquidity touchpoints — own the Payment Ops interface into daily reconciliation across MCA, RTGS DCA and TIPS DCA, and escalate where liquidity affects payment execution or customer outcomes (buffer funding/defunding remains a Finance Ops/Treasury responsibility).

Incident management, contingency and reporting

  • Redesign the incident process for direct participation — replacing BNPP phone/email escalation with DNB, FIS and TARGET detection and escalation routes — and own operational payment-impact assessment.
  • Own the Payment Ops role in DNB notifications and reporting (settlement mismatches, operational incidents) and retain evidence to the DNB readiness standard.
  • Define the Payment Ops role in the Eurosystem contingency solution (ECONS II) for severe TARGET disruption, including training and test evidence.

Cross-functional and external coordination

  • Work directly with the T2 scheme / Eurosystem on certification, registration and reference data, and act as an operational point of contact for DNB, SWIFT / the NSP (NEXI) and the FIS service provider.
  • Handle communications with other banks and correspondents, including BNP Paribas during the dual-run period.
  • Partner directly with the Product and Engineering teams: test interfaces, identify back-office development needs from dashboard testing, and specify what stays automated versus manual — you are the operational voice defining how the platform must behave, and these decisions sit with Ops, not with engineering.
  • Work closely with our reconciliation team on liquidity management and forming operational processes around it

What success looks like

  • Every Payment Ops process for direct participation has a named owner, a documented existing-process-plus-T2-delta, confirmed manual/automated steps, agreed escalation and fallback, and passing UAT evidence, meeting regulatory and customer expectations
  • Full set of T2 procedures established and ownership → recalls, investigations/pacs.028, inbound RTGS credit and Escrow return, rejects, reconciliation, incident and GUI fallback
  • Successful migration from indirect participation to direct, withdocumented and Customer Support equipped with accurate customer-facing guidance, and 0 impact on customer experience
  • Post-go-live, T2 operations run as stable BAU with Finom-controlled investigation SLAs and no residual BNPP operational dependency.

Requirements

  • Experience in payment operations at a bank, EMI or PSP, ideally covering SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst) and TARGET Services with direct connectivity
  • Working knowledge of payment investigations, recalls, returns and SWIFT / ISO 20022 messaging (MT199/MT999, pacs/camt/pain).
  • Comfort operating central-infrastructure interfaces hands-on (T2 GUI, CRDM, reconciliation and liquidity-monitoring tools), including U2A/A2A actions.
  • Strong process design and documentation skills — able to author DNB-ready SOPs, define four-eyes controls and authorization matrices, and produce audit-quality evidence.
  • Confidence coordinating with regulators and external parties (DNB, Eurosystem, SWIFT/NSP, service providers, correspondent banks) and translating operational needs to Product and Engineering.
  • Senior enough to own sign-offs, incident escalation and DNB-reporting decisions independently, while working across Ops, IT/Security, Compliance, Risk and Finance Ops.
  • Familiarity with DNB / TARGET-NL conditions, IPR (Instant Payments Regulation) and EMI/PSD2 operational obligations.

Nice to have

  • Prior involvement in a direct TARGET / RTGS / TIPS onboarding or a sponsor-bank-to-direct-participation migration.
  • Experience standing up incident management and contingency (ECONS II) processes for payment infrastructure.

Prerequisites

  • Minimum 3+ years of experience in payment operations at a bank, EMI, or PSP, with hands-on exposure to SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst) and TARGET Services (T2/RTGS, TIPS) direct connectivity.
  • Practical knowledge of payment investigations, recalls, returns/refunds workflows, and SWIFT / ISO 20022 messaging standards (MT199/MT999, pacs, camt, pain).
  • Demonstrated experience operating central financial-infrastructure interfaces directly (e.g., T2 GUI, CRDM, reconciliation or liquidity-monitoring tools), including U2A/A2A actions.
  • Proven ability to design and document operational processes, including SOPs, four-eyes controls, and authorization matrices to audit/regulatory standard.
  • Experience liaising directly with regulators or scheme operators (e.g., central banks, Eurosystem, SWIFT/NSP) and cross-functional teams such as Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Risk.
  • Seniority sufficient to independently own sign-offs, incident escalation, and regulatory reporting decisions.
  • Familiarity with relevant regulatory frameworks — DNB/TARGET-NL conditions, the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), and EMI/PSD2 operational obligations.
  • Professional fluency in English (written and spoken) for regulatory and cross-border coordination.
